questions.question: Isobars are lines joining places with equal:
Why does a high-pressure cell generally bring clear, settled weather?
options: Because air rises and cools in a high
Because air sinks in a high, warming and drying as it descends
Because highs only occur in summer
Because highs contain no air movement

questions.question: Closely packed isobars on a synoptic chart indicate:
options: Strong winds due to a steep pressure gradient

questions.question: A station circle shaded six-eighths means:
options: Six-eighths of the sky is covered in cloud
There is a 6/8 chance of rain

questions.question: Air temperature 18 °C, dew point 16 °C. What does the small gap tell you?
options: The air is nearly saturated — humid, with condensation or rain close at hand
The station is at high altitude

questions.question: A wind shaft flying into the circle from the north-west with two full feathers represents:
options: A wind blowing toward the north-west at 10 knots

questions.question: Winds are always named according to:
On a synoptic chart a cold front is drawn as a line with:
options: Triangles pointing in the direction the front is moving

questions.question: South African cold fronts typically approach from the:
Why do towering cumulonimbus clouds build along the cold front line?
options: The dense cold air wedges under the warm air and forces it violently upward, where it cools and condenses
The warm air sinks below the cold air
The front blocks all wind movement
High pressure at the front squeezes clouds together

questions.question: Which station-model reading is the classic PRE-frontal picture ahead of a South African cold front?
options: Cold south-westerly wind with clearing skies
Warm, humid north-westerly flow with thickening cloud
Dry air with a 20-degree dew point gap

subtopics.title: The Weather Behind the Front — and the Exam Method

questions.question: Which trio describes the weather BEHIND a cold front?
As a cold front passes a station, the wind typically swings from:
After the front passes, atmospheric pressure at the station:
options: Rises as the low moves away and the next high builds in

questions.question: The lesson's exam method insists that answers be given 'in observations, not vibes'. This means:
options: Quoting the numbers, naming the wind directions, citing the symbols as evidence
Describing how the weather feels emotionally
Avoiding all numbers in your answer
